key_insight: Self-Privileged Fine-Tuning (SPFT) uses a frozen initial model with access to privileged information, such as ground-truth answers, to give greater training weight to tokens predictive of the correct outcome.
engineering_relevance: SPFT offers a token-weighted alternative to standard supervised fine-tuning for adapting language models to mathematical reasoning and code generation.
method: Analyze how dynamic and static token weighting change the target distribution.
Use a frozen initial model conditioned on privileged information to provide token-level weights.
Interpret the weighting through a Bayesian decomposition that favors outcome-predictive tokens.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements over standard SFT and other baselines across the main mathematical reasoning and code generation settings, without specifying benchmarks or effect sizes.
watch_item: Effectiveness depends on the quality of the privileged prior, and generating its token-level weights adds training-pipeline overhead.
